messages.content: what does i will call as soon as i get home say about the time?
it says you plan to call when you get home, without waiting much after that. it does not give an hour unless the time you get home is known.
can i change as soon as to after and keep the same idea?
after keeps the order, but it can leave more time open between getting home and calling. as soon as makes the call sound close to the time you get home.
give me the two examples instead of an explanation.
i will call after i get home. i will call as soon as i get home.
now make the one with as soon as a question to my sister.
will you call as soon as you get home?
what if she says i may call instead of i will call?
then the call is less sure. may call leaves open whether she will do it.
can she be home without calling?
yes. her being home does not make a possible call happen by itself.
now write a message that says i am home but cannot talk yet.
i am home now, but i cannot talk yet. i will call when i am free.
does that give a specific hour?
no. it says the call will be when you are free, not at an hour already given.
the plant by my window has a new leaf. i know that sounds small, but i am happy about it.
it can be good to see something you care for growing. what do you like about this plant?
i like seeing it when i wake up. i do not need it to be the most large plant in the world.
then the new leaf can be something you enjoy on its own, without a very large goal for it.
say that simply.
you can enjoy the new leaf without making a larger goal out of it.
can you help me write a short message to my sister? she gave me the plant.
the plant you gave me has a new leaf. i am happy to see it growing by my window.
she says she is happy too and asks for a picture. i have not taken one yet.
you can say you will send one when you take it, if that is what you want to do.
write that reply without saying i already sent it.
i have not taken a picture yet. i will send one when i do.
what does one mean there?
it is about a picture of the plant.
only give a kind reply to my first message again.
it sounds like a small thing that made you happy.
write a story about two people waiting inside because of rain. they should enjoy the wait without saying rain is always good.

a woman and her cousin were ready to go for a walk when rain began outside. they stood by the door for a moment, then went back to the living room. the cousin found a book of pictures on the shelf and opened it on the table. they looked at places they had visited and places they had never seen. one picture made the woman remember a trip with her father, and she told the story while her cousin listened. after a while, the rain stopped. they closed the book, put it back, and went for their walk. the wait had changed the start of the visit, but it had also given them time for a conversation they had not chosen before.
give me a different last sentence.
they had wanted a walk, but they also enjoyed the time talking inside.
does that say people must enjoy every wait?
no. it is one story about these two people. another wait could feel very different.
who remembered a trip with her father?
the woman.
did they leave the book on the table when they went out?
no. they put it back before going for the walk.
now tell the change of plan in the voice of the cousin.
we waited inside while there was rain, looked at a book together, and went for a walk after it stopped.
only give the place they waited.
in the living room.
what is different between the cup is too full and the cup is full enough?
too full can mean there is more in it than works for what you want to do. full enough can mean there is as much as you need for it.
give the difference in two shorter sentences.
too full can mean more than works for what you want to do. full enough can mean as much as you need for it.
i want to carry water without it going over the top. can too full be about that?
yes. a cup can be too full to carry without water going over the top while you move.
say that with no while at the end.
a cup can be too full to carry without water going over the top.
now i take a little water out. can it still be full enough for the plant?
yes. less water can still be enough if the plant needs only that much.
can you know how much water this plant needs from the word plant alone?
no. different plants can need different care. the general word does not tell us how much water this one needs.
ask a short question about this plant instead.
how much water does this plant need?
now only give an example with enough time instead of water.
i have enough time to read one page before work.
i need a quiet place for a short call. my family is talking in the living room. help me ask without telling everyone to leave the house.
could i have a quiet place for a short call? i do not need everyone to leave, just a little time where i can hear clearly.
what if i could use the bedroom but the door does not close?
then you can ask whether the family could talk quietly for the few minutes of the call, if that would help.
write that question.
could you talk quietly for a few minutes while i have this call?
can i give the reason without saying they always make too much sound?
yes. you can say: i need to hear the person on the phone clearly. could you talk quietly for a few minutes?
now my brother asks how long. i think five minutes, but it might take longer.
then keep that open: i think about five minutes, but i will let you know when i am done.
what if i say five minutes for sure?
that would sound like a more sure time than you know. about five minutes leaves the time more open.
give the message with about.
i think about five minutes, but i will let you know when i am done.
my cousin said she liked the picture i made. i wanted to say thank you, but i started telling her every part i thought was wrong.
you can thank her without a long explanation of every part you want to change. a kind reply does not need an answer about the whole picture.
give me a shorter answer with do not need.
you do not need to explain every part you want to change before saying thank you.
give me a simple sentence i could say.
thank you. i am happy you liked it.
what if i really do want to change part of the drawing later?
you can say thank you now and still choose to change part of the picture later.
say that with part of the picture.
you can say thank you now and still choose to change part of the picture later.
can you help me keep both ideas in one reply?
thank you. i am happy you liked it, even though there are parts i may work on again.
what if that is more than i need?
then thank you. i am happy you liked it is enough.
just give that short reply.
thank you. i am happy you liked it.
write a story about a parent visiting a school. do not give the school a name, and do not choose a town.

a mother came to the school to see the work her child had made. a teacher met her near the door and showed her to a room with pictures on the wall. the child stood by one picture of a house and a garden. he told his mother why he had chosen that color and where the idea had come from. she listened, then asked about the small tree near the house. he said it was like the tree near the home of his grandmother. before leaving, the mother looked at a few other pictures with him. they walked out together, still talking about what he wanted to draw next.
give me only the sentence about the color.
he told his mother why he had chosen that color and where the idea had come from.
did the story say this was a real picture of the home of his grandmother?
no. he said the tree was like one near her home. that does not make the whole house and garden the same place.
now make the last part a conversation between them with only one reply from each.
child: next time, i want to draw the tree by itself. mother: i would like to hear about it when you do.
can you keep the mother from choosing what he must draw?
yes. her reply says she would like to hear about his choice, not that he must make a specific picture.
just give her reply again.
i would like to hear about it when you do.
use whether in a sentence about choosing to walk or stay home.
i have not chosen whether to walk or stay home.
does that say i will do both?
no. it leaves a choice between the two. it does not say you will do both.
now make it a question i can ask myself.
should i walk or stay home?
that does not have whether. can you give a question with whether without making it sound hard?
have i chosen whether to walk or stay home?
what if i want to ask my brother about his choice?
have you chosen whether to walk or stay home?
he says he wants to walk but not alone. what could i ask next?
would you like me to walk with you?
can you say i already said yes to go?
no. asking whether he would like you to join is not the same as already saying yes.
what if i do want to go with him?
then you can say: i would like to walk with you.
only give the first whether sentence again.
i have not chosen whether to walk or stay home.
i did not do much today. i read a little, made lunch, and had a long talk with my sister. i keep saying i did nothing.
those are things you did, even if they were not part of a large task. reading, making lunch, and talking with your sister can all be parts of a day.
i think i only count things if i can say they were work.
then you may be leaving out parts of life that are still important to you. did you enjoy the talk with your sister?
yes. we had not had much time together this week.
that sounds like time you wanted, not nothing. you can talk about the day without making it a test of how much work you finished.
write it in my voice.
i had a slow day. i read a little, made lunch, and spent time talking with my sister. i did not finish a large work task, but i did things that were important to me.
can i leave out the part about a work task?
yes. i had a slow day. i read a little, made lunch, and had a long talk with my sister.
what if i want only one sentence?
i had a slow day with a little reading, making lunch, and a long talk with my sister.
does that say where i made lunch?
no. it gives the things you did, without choosing the place where you made lunch.
give a kind reply to my first message now.
you did more than nothing, even if the day was quiet.
write a story about where a book goes through a day, but do not make the book think or talk.

in the morning, a girl took a book from the shelf and put it on the kitchen table. she read while waiting for breakfast, then carried it to school. during a quiet part of the day, she showed a picture in it to a friend. after school, the book came home with her and sat on the chair while she helped her father with dinner. later, her brother asked if he could read it next. she said yes, but wanted to finish one last page first. after reading that page, she gave it to him. he took the book to his room, where it stayed open on his desk until it was time for bed.
where was the book while she helped with dinner?
on the chair at home.
who had it after she finished the last page?
her brother.
did the book choose to go to his room?
no. he carried it there. you asked for the book not to think or talk.
can you tell the end in the voice of the brother?
my sister gave me the book after finishing her last page. i took it to my room and read at my desk until it was time for bed.
what if the last page was only the last one she wanted that day, not the end of the whole book?
then the original story can leave that open. finishing one last page does not have to mean finishing the whole book.
now only give the last known place of the book.
on the desk in the room of the brother.
what is different between someone is at the door and is anyone at the door?
someone is at the door says a person is there. is anyone at the door asks whether a person is there.
now say nobody is there.
nobody is at the door.
does nobody mean i do not know who the person is?
no. nobody says no person is there. not knowing who is there is different.
make a sentence about a person being there but their name not being known.
someone is at the door, but i do not know who it is.
can you ask for that name without saying nobody?
who is at the door?
now use anyone in a request for help.
can anyone help me carry these books?
does that mean every person must help?
no. it asks whether someone can help. it does not say every person must do it.
if one person helps, can i say nobody helped?
no. one person helping makes nobody helped false.
just give the request with books again.
can anyone help me carry these books?
my friend asks why i am not coming for the walk we often take together. i need to work today, but i do not want her to think i will stop all our walks.
i cannot come for the walk today because i need to work. i would like to walk together another day.
can you keep it without choosing a next day for us?
yes. that message leaves another day open without choosing one.
give me only the message.
i cannot come for the walk today because i need to work. i would like to walk together another day.
she asks if i no longer like walking with her.
you can say you still like it, and today is about work rather than the walk itself.
write that in a kind way.
i still like walking with you. i just need to work today.
what if tomorrow i have time, but i do not know her plan?
then you can ask whether tomorrow would work for her, rather than say the walk is already chosen.
write that question only.
would tomorrow work for a walk together?
does it have to be a long walk?
not from that question. you can choose how long together if she wants to go.
which is more clear: he put it there, or my father put the book on the table?
my father put the book on the table is more clear without other context, because it gives the person, object, and place.
can he put it there be enough in a conversation?
yes. if both people already know who he is, what it is, and where there is, the short sentence can be enough.
give a short conversation where it works.
person: where is the book? friend: your father was carrying it. person: did he put it on the table? friend: yes, he put it there.
can you give it without person and friend at the start of each part?
where is the book? your father was carrying it. did he put it on the table? yes, he put it there.
can you make it even shorter and keep the table clear?
did your father put the book on the table? yes, he put it there.
what makes there clear in that example?
the question gave the table as the place.
say that with there can point to it.
the question gave the table as the place, so there can point to it.
only give the long sentence again.
my father put the book on the table.
my friend waited while i finished a call. i want to thank her without saying it took hours, because it was only a few minutes.
thank you for waiting while i finished the call.
can i say i know waiting had no useful task for her?
you can keep it simple without choosing her feeling: thank you for waiting. i am ready now.
what if she says she was happy reading her book?
then you can listen to what she said about her time with the book. you do not need to keep saying it must have been hard.
write a reply to her.
i am happy you had your book with you. thank you for waiting.
does that make the wait a good thing for everyone every time?
no. it is about this wait and what your friend said about it.
now give a short thank you.
thank you for waiting.
can i use that even if i only took one minute?
yes. a short wait can still be something you thank someone for.
only that reply again.
thank you for waiting.
write a story where a girl thinks her brother took her book, but she finds it herself. keep the brother kind, and do not make her lie.

a girl wanted to read after lunch, but her book was not on the table where she remembered leaving it. she saw her brother by the shelf and asked whether he had taken it. he said he had not, but said he could help her look. she checked the kitchen while he looked near the sofa. then she remembered taking the book to the window that morning. it was still on the chair there, under a garment she had put down. she told her brother she had found it and said thank you for helping. he said he was happy it was not lost. they sat down near each other, each with a book, and read for a while.
give only the part about him helping and her saying thank you.
he said he had not taken it, but said he could help her look. later, she told him she had found it and said thank you for helping.
was her first thought a lie?
she could think he took it and still be wrong. a lie would be saying something she knew was false.
say it more simply.
she could think he took it and still be wrong. a lie would be saying something she knew was false.
what did she do when she found out where it was?
she told him she had found it and said thank you for helping.
can you give a short sentence she could say without saying he had taken it?
i found my book by the window. thank you for helping me look.
now only give the place she found it.
on the chair by the window, under a garment.
what does he looked as if he was tired say?
it gives how he looked, without saying we know for sure he was tired.
say it with looked and know for sure.
it gives how he looked, without saying we know for sure he was tired.
what if he then says i am just thinking, not tired?
then you have his own words about it. you can say he told you he was thinking rather than tired.
can i keep saying he must be tired just because he was quiet?
quiet alone does not tell you that for sure. he has given a different answer.
say that using only quiet alone.
quiet alone does not tell you he is tired for sure. he has told you he is thinking.
now use as if in a story about a child playing a teacher.
a child stood by the table and spoke as if he was the teacher.
does that make him the real teacher?
no. as if keeps it as how he spoke or what he was playing, not his real work.
now only give the first sentence about tired.
he looked as if he was tired.
my mother left a cup of tea on my desk while i was working. she did not say anything, but it felt kind.
that sounds like a small way she showed care while you were busy.
i want to thank her, but a long message would be too much for a cup of tea.
a simple thank you can be enough. thank you for the tea. it was kind of you.
can i say it helped me have a little break?
yes, if that is what it did for you. thank you for the tea. it helped me take a little break.
what if i want to keep both kind and break?
thank you for the tea. it was kind of you and helped me take a little break.
does that sound like a letter instead of something i can say in the kitchen?
you could say it more simply: thanks for the tea. it was a nice little break.
give the short reply only.
thanks for the tea. it was a nice little break.
now say something warm about my first message without writing for me.
it sounds like a small moment of care in a busy day.
write a story where a child asks why an old house is empty, and the parent does not know. do not add a reason just to make a large problem in the story.

a child walked past an old house with her father. the door was closed, and nobody was near it. she asked why no one lived there. her father said he did not know whether it was empty or whether the people were simply away. they stood for a moment looking at the garden, then kept walking. the child thought about the house as they went home. later, she drew it with an open door and a person in the garden. in her picture, she could choose a story, even though she still did not know the real reason the place had looked quiet.
did the father know no one lived there?
no. he did not know whether it was empty or the people were away.
was the person in the garden a real person they saw?
no. the child added that person in her drawing.
can you tell the difference in one sentence?
the real house looked quiet, but the child could choose people and a story for her picture.
now make the last part in the voice of the child.
i drew the house with an open door and a person in the garden, even though i did not know who really lived there.
only give what the father knew about why it looked quiet.
he did not know the reason.
which sounds right: a blue small cup or a small blue cup?
a small blue cup is the right word order for this simple example.
give only the correct example.
a small blue cup.
now use book, old, and red.
an old red book.
why an instead of a?
it is about the first sound in old. an old book is right for that example.
give two examples, one with old and one with red.
an old book. a red book.
can i say the old red book if we already know which one?
yes. the can help make it the specific book already clear in the conversation.
what if i have two old red books?
then those words alone may not make the choice clear. you might need a detail such as on the table or in my hand.
write a request for the one on the table.
please bring the old red book on the table.
now only give the example with cup again.
a small blue cup.
that message is good. i can use it as it is. please do not keep making more messages.
okay. we can keep that one.
can you say something warm without asking what i will do next?
i hope the conversation goes well.
now just goodbye.
goodbye.
can you add take care, with no other sentence?
goodbye. take care.
only one sentence this time.
goodbye, and take care.
